notes: The mechanical assertions (1-5, 8, 9, 11, 13) are all checked by check_run.py and were trivially green here; they would also pass a thin but well-formed doc set, so the discriminating power sits in 6, 7, 10 and 12. Assertion 7 names five facts but the specs assert many more (error message strings, output line formats, key ordering, exit codes); a wrong message string or the CLI-006 'left-padded' slip would go uncaught, so consider extending 7 to the error messages and output formats, or adding a 'no false fact in any spec' assertion. The skim test is the only judgment assertion that caught anything, and it caught a one-sentence teaser that the prose linter does not detect; if the linter grew a teaser rule ('Two things ...', 'N principles ...') this would become mechanical. No assertion covers whether the proposal records the scope trade-offs (SLA folded into tickets, P9 traceback as TODO), which this run did well and which distinguishes a thoughtful bootstrap from a template fill.
